card.description: The fixed CSS stabilizer block introduced by Shor: three inner bit-flip repetition blocks become the symbols of an outer phase-flip repetition code. Short Z checks locate X components inside a block, long X checks locate Z components between blocks, and a Y fault activates both syndrome sectors.

views.description: Six Z rows are three disjoint copies of the length-three open-chain parity matrix. Two X rows are the outer length-three parity matrix with each bit expanded across one complete inner block. This executable row order fixes every syndrome and normalizer statement on the entry.

In the encoded-basis convention, logical X is Z on one site in each inner block and logical Z is X across any complete block. Both have weight three, commute with every stabilizer, lie outside its row space, and anticommute with each other.

The inner bit-flip code compares neighboring computational-basis bits. The outer phase-flip code compares the phase of neighboring cat-state blocks. A single Y fault has both components, so its syndrome is the XOR of the two repetition decisions rather than a third decoding problem.

The constructor-derived bipartite incidence view places data in three rows. Six short Z-check spokes stay within rows, while two long X-check spokes join adjacent rows. The geometry is a block-structure diagram, not a claim of hardware locality.

The square three-by-three Bacon–Shor subsystem block recovers this stabilizer presentation by promoting its horizontal ZZ gauge pairs to stabilizers while retaining its two X center generators. The directed typed edge therefore runs from Bacon–Shor to Shor; this stabilizer code does not carry the discarded gauge subsystem.

A suitable projective-plane cellulation realizes the same stabilizer subspace as a homological code. This supplies a topological dictionary for the fixed block, not an identity edge to every projective-plane code or a new scalable family claim.

General stabilizer-to-graph conversion can encode an equivalent tableau as graph data after local Clifford bookkeeping. A graph state is not by itself the Shor code: the logical subspace and the equivalence map must remain explicit.

The parameter label [[9,1,3]] does not identify this code uniquely. Other nine-qubit stabilizer constructions can be inequivalent, so an identity claim needs a stabilizer or encoded-basis equivalence witness rather than a matching parameter tuple.

decoders.noise: one fixed block under a single-qubit Pauli fault, perfect readout of the eight stabilizers, and correction modulo stabilizer degeneracy
decoders.notes: Decode an X component from the two adjacent-pair Z syndromes inside its block, then decode a Z component from the two long X syndromes between blocks; a Y component triggers both decisions. The rule may be stored as a finite syndrome table or executed as two nested repetition decisions. It is not an asymptotic threshold claim. Under coherent correlated idling, stabilizer-sector interference changes the likelihood model, so the independent-Pauli table is not a model-free decoder.

realizations.description: The fixed Shor block was directly encoded and its prepared logical states were characterized on a trapped-ion processor. This establishes an encoder and fixed-block state preparation, not repeated fault-tolerant syndrome cycles or an increasing-distance memory threshold.

A sign-adjusted distance-three Shor-code sector was implemented and compared under correlated coherent idling. The result is specific to the chosen stabilizer eigenvalues, noise Hamiltonian, and fixed block; it is not a model-independent improvement of the canonical code space.

A photonic nine-qubit Shor state was prepared, while generalized Shor blocks supplied loss protection inside the larger repeater protocol. State preparation and loss-tolerant repeater behavior are distinct from repeated arbitrary-Pauli correction by this fixed memory block.

relations.how: Three length-three bit-flip repetition blocks are the physical symbols of a length-three phase-flip repetition code. At matrix level, H_Z is three block-diagonal copies of the open repetition parity matrix and H_X is the outer parity matrix expanded across complete inner blocks. This is a curated construction relation: the repository has no exact concatenation replay adapter, so this card deliberately omits a construction recipe instead of presenting the relation as verifier evidence.

operations.gate: logical Pauli X and Z representatives
operations.cost: one parallel layer on three data qubits: Z on one site in every inner block for logical X, or X across one complete block for logical Z; equivalent representatives follow by stabilizer multiplication

operations.gate: CNOT between two fixed Shor blocks
operations.cost: one layer of nine pairwise physical CNOTs; with the declared encoded-basis logical names, the physical arrows point from the logical target block toward the logical control block. Routing, syndrome extraction, and recovery before or after the layer are additional resources.

origin.method: binary CNOT conjugation of constructor logical representatives
